deities: Lord Shiva as Sri Kapileswara (Swayambhu lingam)
festivals: Kapileswara Swamy Brahmotsavams (nine-day, February; the biggest festival, conducted by TTD)
Kartika Purnima Mukkoti (merging of the teerthas, when a holy dip is believed to grant salvation)

history.period: Vijayanagara patronage 13th-16th centuries (Saluva Narasimha Deva Raya to Sri Krishna Deva Raya and later rulers); legendary origin far older
history.summary: The Sri Kapileswara Swamy Temple stands at the foothills of the Seshachala range in Tirupati, with the Kapila Theertham waterfall flowing into its holy pond. Legend holds that the sage Kapila performed penance to Shiva here; Shiva and Parvati appeared, and the Shiva lingam is believed to be self-manifested (Swayambhu). The temple received strong patronage from the Vijayanagara rulers of the 13th-16th centuries, especially Saluva Narasimha Deva Raya, Sri Krishna Deva Raya, and later rulers like Venkatapathi Raya and Aliya Ramaraya. Today it is administered by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) and is the only major Shiva temple in the Tirupati area, renowned for its annual Brahmotsavams. Note: there is a second, smaller Avilala Kapileswara Swamy temple nearby (approx. 13.61, 79.42); this record is the main TTD temple at Kapila Theertham (coords corroborated by tourism.intirupati.com's 13.656228, 79.42124).

name: Sri Kapileswara Swamy Temple
town_description: Tirupati, at the foot of the Seshachala hills in southern Andhra Pradesh, is one of India's great pilgrimage cities, anchored by the Sri Venkateswara Temple on the Tirumala hills. It draws tens of millions of devotees a year and has its own international airport, a major rail junction, and a dense network of city buses and autos serving its temples.

travel.airport: Tirupati International Airport at Renigunta (approx. 14-15 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Tirupati railway station (approx. 3 km), well connected across South India.
travel.road: City buses and autos run from Tirupati town to Kapila Theertham (approx. 3 km northwest of the city centre); the temple sits at the base of the Tirumala ghat road.

visitor_information.best_time: November to February for pleasant weather. The nine-day Brahmotsavams in February is the most festive time. Kartika month (October-November), especially Kartika Purnima Mukkoti, is highly auspicious.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Generally 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily (verify — sources conflict on midday breaks: one guide lists sarva darshanam blocks approx. 7:00-11:00 AM, 11:30 AM-4:00 PM and 6:30-8:00 PM, another lists morning darshan 5:00 AM-12:00 noon and evening 4:00-8:00 PM; timings shift during festivals).
